dossiers.title: Skyborn
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 8 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Traditional turn-based party battles have visible map enemies rather than random encounters; players can often avoid routine fights and concentrate on story or optional challenging battles.
The illustrated characters, music and concise steampunk-fantasy story are praised by players as polished and engaging for an RPG Maker production.
The plot advances briskly between dungeons, but repeated encounters along lengthy corridors interrupt narrative momentum and can feel monotonous.
Optional bosses, character builds and difficulty settings change how demanding the combat feels; some found a late encounter sudden or difficult while others considered battles too easy.
Crafting, equipment, class development and arena battles offer side progression, although thin shop inventories and unclear stat descriptions limit the appeal of experimentation.
Russian and English reviewers describe inconvenient equipment management, limited control customization and little explanation of exactly what some ability or gear attributes accomplish.
A story-only playthrough can be quite short, while optional content and higher difficulty can push completion beyond ten hours, splitting opinion on whether the adventure has enough scope.
A Russian player points to a community-made translation rather than an official Russian-language release; reliance on an unofficial patch may be an accessibility concern.

conflicts.statement: Some appreciate Skyborn as a focused RPG with little compulsory grinding, whereas others consider the runtime too short or the corridor encounters repetitive.

dossiers.title: Massacre At The Mirage
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Players describe a compact first-person interactive slasher in which switching between cinema employees and other victims takes precedence over constant survival combat.
Day-to-day cinema duties, serving customers and small mini-games fill the spaces between narrative killings; these repeated chores divide opinion on how much there is to play.
Neon cinema visuals, retro slasher references, voice performances and elaborately staged kills receive praise, although not every player finds the same campy writing convincing.
The core plot lasts about two to four hours for reviewed players; some value its one-evening cinematic focus, while others wanted more interactive action and less filler.
An unlockable snack-counter simulation adds decorations and collectibles but demands enough repeated service shifts that achievement-focused players may grow bored.
Dissatisfied players point to prolonged mundane tasks, simple puzzles and the lack of meaningful control during scenes, turning a potentially tense slasher story into passive watching.
A dated Russian player review complains about missing Russian localization, independent of the player's positive impression of the genre premise.
Horror reactions vary: some enjoy the killer's stylized brutality and Halloween mood, whereas a Russian critic found the plot predictable and the presentation insufficiently frightening.
A player on the alternate storefront reports sections so dark they had to increase gamma, while still praising the atmosphere, mini-games and playable viewpoints.

conflicts.statement: Routine ticket and snack tasks and passive cinematic sequences are praised as authentic slasher-film framing by some viewers but criticized as slow padding by others.

dossiers.title: Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Ground-focused real-time warfare revolves around a mobile carrier that constructs units, performs research and retains forces between campaign missions, making fleet preservation matter.
Flanking through desert terrain, coordinating unit groups and using tactical zoom to plan battles provide satisfying RTS play, though unit variety can feel constrained.
Players praise radio chatter, sweeping desert visuals, music and prequel lore for creating a distinctive military-science-fiction expedition atmosphere.
The single-player campaign is gripping for several players but quite short, with scripted mission encounters and limited motivation to replay once the story ends.
Players criticize unchangeable keybindings and tactical overlays that obstruct information during busy battles, complicating otherwise enjoyable large-scale control.
Some campaign players find the highest difficulty surprisingly manageable, whereas others report frustrating enemy waves and tactical resource limitations.
An older player report finds public multiplayer matches hard to discover, so this game should not be treated as a dependable drop-in multiplayer experience.

Russian and English Steam players criticize the addition of Epic Online Services and report service/launch friction; these complaints are dated and do not establish that every installation is currently broken.
A Russian player report dated December 2025 describes a launch where the campaign and settings controls did not respond, blocking play for that installation.

A Russian-speaking participant in the game's official community complained that subtitles alone were difficult to keep up with and wanted full voice localization; this is historical rather than evidence of a current localization failure.

conflicts.statement: The atmospheric and story-rich RTS campaign earns praise while players differ on tactical depth, control responsiveness and whether later added service dependencies undermine use of the game.
